CA.text: Every employer with one or more employees must carry workers’ compensation; a roofing business with no employees must be insured too.

FL.text: Construction: from one employee, corporate officers counted. Other industries: from 4 employees. Agriculture: 6 regular or 12 seasonal workers.

WI.text: Three or more employees, or a single employee paid $500 or more in a calendar quarter; farmers from 6 employees on 20 days of a year.

TX.text: Private employers can choose to carry coverage, but it is not required in most cases; an employer without it (a non-subscriber) must report to the state that it has no coverage.

SD.text: No South Dakota law requires an employer to carry workers’ compensation; an uninsured employer may be sued in civil court by an injured worker.

GA.text: Three or more persons regularly employed, part-time or full time; the State Board may assess a civil penalty of $500 to $5,000 per occurrence on an employer that fails to provide coverage.

MO.text: Five or more employees; in construction, from one employee.

SC.text: Exempt with fewer than 4 employees, or with a total payroll under $3,000 in the previous year.

VA.text: Exempt with fewer than 3 employees regularly in service; farm workers exempt unless more than 3 work full time.

KS.text: Exempt with a gross annual payroll of $20,000 or less last year and expected this year, wages of family members left out.

MT.text: All employers, with listed exceptions such as household work, casual work, family members and owners.

CO.text: Every business with employees, whatever their number.

HI.text: One or more employees, full time or part time.

AZ.text: Anyone who employs regular employees, domestic workers excepted.

PA.text: Required for most employers; domestic workers optional; farm workers exempt when they work fewer than 30 days or earn less than $1,200 in a year from one employer.

WA.text: Every employer with workers, through the state fund of Labor & Industries or self-insurance: private insurers are not allowed.
